# hw1 human-written replication (generated by src/analyze_hw1.py)

Run hw1: 4 models, P0, 5 channels, judged + blind-arbitrated, attributed without fallback (0 unresolved). Analysed: 546 of 547 kept families (primary exclusions: 1: the P06 speech-act pair per D-058 and any refusal/acceptance speech-act family, as in W-C). Bootstrap: 10000 cluster resamples, seed 20261031, W-C estimator (`analyze.family_bootstrap`); primary clusters = writer_id.

Families by dimension: {'polarity': 104, 'agent': 102, 'time_quantity': 97, 'politeness': 89, 'certainty': 87, 'speech_act': 67}. Writers by dimension: {'agent': 7, 'certainty': 6, 'polarity': 7, 'politeness': 6, 'speech_act': 6, 'time_quantity': 7}. **Each contrast rests on only 5-7 writers; writer-cluster percentile CIs with so few clusters are unstable and probably too narrow at the tails (P1: the speech-act subset).**

## Integrity
Recomputed vs stored attribution agreement: {'critical_match': 1.0, 'violation': 1.0, 'commitment': 1.0}.


## Interpretation (hand-written; numbers from the tables above)

- All three registered contrasts replicate in direction and Holm decision, and the point estimates sit at or slightly above W-C (P1 +35.3 vs +31.4 pp; P2 +7.6 vs +6.3; P3 99.8% vs 99.4% affirmative). The writer-cluster CIs overlap the W-C CIs.
- Treat the writer-cluster CIs as optimistic. Each contrast has only 6-7 writers; with so few clusters the percentile bootstrap is coarse, the p-values sit at the resampling floor (1/10001, Holm x3 = 0.0003), and for P1 the writer CI [31.3, 40.3] is not wider than the family CI [31.0, 39.4], which is not credible as a precision claim. The W-C CIs (55 and 80 clusters) are the better-conditioned ones. The direction (P1 > 0 in all four models, P3 near 50 pp, P2 >= 0 in all four) is the robust statement; the interval widths are not.
- P2 is concentrated: gemma3-4b +22.5 pp, gpt-6.1-terra +6.7, llama +1.1, qwen 0.0. The pooled +7.6 is a model-mix average, as in W-C.
- P1 by model ranges +18.7 (llama) to +50.7 (gpt-6.1-terra). Speech-act chipall is much better here than in W-C (91.0% vs 74.8% match; Llama 85% vs 49%), so the W-C finding that extra chips hurt speech act llama does not replicate on human-written pairs; the cause was not investigated.
- Polarity and politeness bare/noncrit match 50% by design (both variants share one bare input); the informative quantities there are the chip gain and the assumption rate, not the match rate.
- Agent chip gain (67.3 pp) is larger than main1's (52.5 pp, 10 families): human writers' bare inputs commit to "speaker" less often (assumption on noncrit 98.5% vs 100%). Time and certainty replicate main1 within its wide CIs.
- Sensitivities: nothing changes a conclusion. Near-duplicate collapse, P06 exclusion and the arbiter reversals move estimates by at most 1.7 pp. All 574 candidates lowers P1 to +30.9 [25.3, 35.0] (4.4 pp, the only shift over 2 pp); Holm decisions are unchanged. The 'Sure,' reversal cannot move critical match by codebook (plain assertion is honoured by plain or emphatic); it only moves the emphatic share of chip1/chipall outputs for plain-assertion targets (81.2% -> 79.7%, within CI).
